module.title: Tooth Identification and Localization
module.goal: Establish fluency in identifying and localizing teeth across radiographic views using morphology, position

objectives.text: Correctly identify teeth on bitewing and periapical radiographs using the Universal numbering system with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly determine whether a radiograph shows the right or left side of the mouth with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly determine whether a radiograph is maxillary or mandibular with ≥85% accuracy
Use tooth shape, root structure, and position within the arch to distinguish between similar teeth on radiographs with ≥80% accuracy
Correctly identify adjacent teeth and tooth relationships on radiographs with ≥90% accuracy
Identify missing, restored, impacted, or malpositioned teeth on radiographs with ≥90% accuracy

cases.name: Mandibular Left First Molar
cases.finding: A single posterior tooth with two roots is highlighted on a periapical radiograph.

steps.prompt: Is the highlighted tooth in the maxillary or mandibular arch?
steps.feedback: Two roots (one mesial, one distal) and the dense inferior cortex place this in the mandible.

steps.prompt: Using standard mounting (the patient's right is on your left), which side of the mouth is this?
steps.feedback: With the patient's right on your left, this molar sits on the patient's left side.

steps.prompt: Identify the highlighted tooth (Universal numbering system).
steps.feedback: The first molar is the largest posterior tooth with two well-separated roots — #19 in the lower left.

steps.prompt: Which feature best supports that identification?
options: Two roots — one mesial, one distal
Three roots including a palatal root
Roots projecting into the maxillary sinus
steps.expected: Two roots — one mesial, one distal
steps.feedback: Mandibular molars have two roots; maxillary molars have three (two buccal + one palatal).

steps.prompt: Which neighbouring tooth is indicated?
steps.feedback: Moving toward the midline from #19 is the second premolar #20; distally is the second molar #18.

cases.name: Maxillary Right First Molar
cases.finding: A large posterior tooth with multiple roots is highlighted near a large radiolucent space.

steps.prompt: Is the highlighted tooth in the maxillary or mandibular arch?
steps.feedback: Three roots (two buccal + one palatal) and superimposition of the maxillary sinus indicate the maxilla.

steps.prompt: Using standard mounting (the patient's right is on your left), which side of the mouth is this?
steps.feedback: With standard mounting, this molar lies on the patient's right side.

steps.prompt: Identify the highlighted tooth (Universal numbering system).
steps.feedback: The largest maxillary posterior tooth with three roots is the first molar — #3 on the upper right.

steps.prompt: Which feature best supports that identification?
options: Three roots — two buccal and one palatal
steps.expected: Three roots — two buccal and one palatal
steps.feedback: Three roots (with a palatal root) and sinus superimposition are hallmarks of a maxillary molar.

steps.prompt: Which neighbouring tooth is indicated?
steps.feedback: Distal to the first molar #3 (away from the midline) is the second molar #2; mesial is #4.

cases.name: Maxillary Right Canine
cases.finding: A single anterior tooth with a notably long root is highlighted.

steps.prompt: Is the highlighted tooth in the maxillary or mandibular arch?
steps.feedback: The long single root and its position in the anterior maxilla identify a maxillary canine.

steps.prompt: Using standard mounting (the patient's right is on your left), which side of the mouth is this?
steps.feedback: In standard mounting this canine is on the patient's right.

steps.prompt: Identify the highlighted tooth (Universal numbering system).
steps.feedback: The canine has the longest root and a single pointed cusp — #6 in the upper right.

steps.prompt: Which feature best supports that identification?
options: The longest single root and a pointed cusp
Two roots and a broad crown
A short root with three cusps
A flat incisal edge and no cusp
steps.expected: The longest single root and a pointed cusp
steps.feedback: Canines have the longest root of any tooth and one prominent cusp tip.

steps.prompt: Which neighbouring tooth is indicated?
steps.feedback: The canine sits between the lateral incisor (#7, mesial) and the first premolar (#5, distal).

cases.name: Mandibular Right First Premolar
cases.finding: A single-rooted posterior tooth with two cusps is highlighted.

steps.prompt: Is the highlighted tooth in the maxillary or mandibular arch?
steps.feedback: The single root and lower-arch trabecular pattern place this in the mandible.

steps.prompt: Using standard mounting (the patient's right is on your left), which side of the mouth is this?
steps.feedback: Standard mounting puts this premolar on the patient's right.

steps.prompt: Identify the highlighted tooth (Universal numbering system).
steps.feedback: A single-rooted, two-cusped tooth just distal to the canine is the first premolar — #28.

steps.prompt: Which feature best supports that identification?
options: A single root and typically two cusps
The longest root in the arch
A large crown with four or more cusps
steps.expected: A single root and typically two cusps
steps.feedback: Premolars have one root and two cusps; molars are larger with multiple roots and cusps.

steps.prompt: Which neighbouring tooth is indicated?
steps.feedback: Distal to #28 is the second premolar #29; mesial is the canine #27.

cases.name: Impacted Third Molar
cases.finding: A posterior tooth is tilted mesially and lodged beneath the adjacent molar, unable to erupt.

steps.prompt: Is the highlighted tooth in the maxillary or mandibular arch?
steps.feedback: The angle of impaction against the second molar and the mandibular canal nearby indicate the lower arch.

steps.prompt: Using standard mounting (the patient's right is on your left), which side of the mouth is this?
steps.feedback: In standard mounting this third molar is on the patient's left.

steps.prompt: Identify the highlighted tooth (Universal numbering system).
steps.feedback: The most posterior mandibular tooth on the left is the third molar — #17.

steps.prompt: How would you classify the highlighted tooth?
steps.feedback: A third molar tilted against the second molar and unable to erupt is impacted (here, mesioangular).

cases.name: Restored Maxillary Molar
cases.finding: A sharply-defined radiopaque material fills the crown of a maxillary posterior tooth.

steps.prompt: Is the highlighted tooth in the maxillary or mandibular arch?
steps.feedback: Three roots and sinus proximity identify a maxillary molar.

steps.prompt: Using standard mounting (the patient's right is on your left), which side of the mouth is this?
steps.feedback: In standard mounting this molar is on the patient's left.

steps.prompt: Identify the highlighted tooth (Universal numbering system).
steps.feedback: A three-rooted maxillary molar in the upper left first-molar position is #14.

steps.prompt: How would you classify the highlighted tooth?
steps.feedback: A well-defined radiopaque mass conforming to a cavity outline is a restoration; untreated caries is radiolucent.
